questions.q: What are the four criteria LTV Global uses to score a candidate critical data element?
options: Number of users, server cost, and uptime
Regulatory, financial, decision, and operational impact
Alphabetical order of the column name
Color, size, popularity, and age
questions.explain: The lesson scores each candidate element against exactly these four impact criteria to decide whether it earns elevated governance.

questions.q: Why did Customers.Email score high enough to become a CDE?
options: It is the longest column name in the schema
It has no relationship to any real-world problem
It only matters to the IT department
It scored high on regulatory impact and is the exact element behind the Lesson 1 DSAR incident
questions.explain: Email is personal data under UK/California privacy law and was the specific element at the center of the access-request gap from Lesson 1.

questions.q: Why did Orders.OrderTotal qualify as a critical data element?
options: It is stored in the Beacon CRM
It feeds the financial and board-level revenue number, scoring high on financial and decision impact
It has no numeric values
It is only used internally by IT for testing
questions.explain: OrderTotal rolls up into the revenue figure Finance reports to the board, which is a direct financial and decision-impact justification.

questions.q: Why did Customers.MarketingOptIn NOT make the CDE list, despite being a real, used column?
options: CDE status is assigned alphabetically
It doesn't exist in any LTV Global system
Getting it wrong risks an unwanted email, not a regulatory finding or board-level number, so it didn't score high on any of the four criteria
Every single column at LTV Global is automatically a CDE
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly contrasts MarketingOptIn's low-stakes failure mode against the four CDEs' regulatory, financial, decision, or operational exposure.

questions.q: Why did Payments.CardToken qualify as a critical data element?
options: It is the most frequently updated column in Atlas
It sits inside PCI scope regardless of how rarely it's queried, scoring high on regulatory impact
It has the highest financial impact of all five candidates
It is stored only in Comet, not Atlas
questions.explain: The lesson notes CardToken scores high on regulatory impact specifically because of PCI scope, independent of query frequency.
